hero.headline: West Palm Beach man to cheer Cape Verde at World Cup in Miami
hero.body:
Eridjon Dacruz of West Palm Beach is traveling to Miami this month to watch Cape Verde compete in the World Cup, marking a historic moment for one of the world's smallest nations to ever qualify for the tournament. Dacruz grew up in Cape Verde, an archipelago consisting of 10 islands located off the African coast, and later relocated to the United States. The island nation, which gained independence from Portugal during the 1970s, has a population of approximately half a million people. As Dacruz prepared for the big game, he looked through his collection of soccer jerseys, pulling out his favorite national team gear from his home country.

Cape Verdeans have expressed tremendous excitement about their national team, called the Tubarão Azul or Blue Sharks, qualifying for the World Cup for the first time in history. Dacruz, who still has many family members living in Cape Verde, noted that the qualification has been a major topic of conversation throughout the islands. He expressed amazement at the achievement, saying he never thought it would happen during his lifetime given the country's small size. When reflecting on his past gaming experiences, Dacruz recalled searching for Cape Verde players in FIFA video games and finding only about two options available. He is confident in his team's potential, believing they can advance if they win a couple of matches.

Dacruz's trip comes courtesy of his girlfriend, who gave him World Cup tickets as an anniversary gift. During their anniversary dinner, she presented him with a handwritten note inside a small box that read "I'm going to the World Cup," surprising him completely. He will attend Cape Verde's match against Uruguay in Miami. The team opens the tournament against Spain, one of the tournament favorites. While waiting for his new Cape Verde national jersey to arrive in time for the game, Dacruz anticipates showing his support in person.

Cape Verde's World Cup qualification will provide significant financial benefits to the nation's soccer development. The soccer federation will receive more than 10 million dollars to help build the next generation of players. Beyond sports, Cape Verde remains frequently mentioned during hurricane season, when tropical systems form near the islands before tracking across the Atlantic toward the United States, according to meteorologist Sami Squires. These weather systems originating from the African coast occasionally develop into storms that move westward across the ocean, though forecasters hope major storms will stay away this year.

cards.headline: 6.1 magnitude earthquake off Cuba rattles Florida from Miami to Jacksonville, prompts evacuations
cards.teaser: A 6.1 magnitude earthquake struck about 73 miles northwest of western Cuba on Monday afternoon at 2 p.m., rattling residents across Florida from Miami and Fort .
cards.body:
A 6.1 magnitude earthquake off the west-northwest coast of Cuba prompted evacuations of several buildings across Miami on Tuesday and was felt as far north as Jacksonville. Students at Fusion Academy were among those evacuated. "The people that are in the top floors, which they said that they felt it even more than we did," student Maria Torrado said. She described the evacuation alarm as urgent, recalling that staff announced "this is not a drill." Streets near some affected buildings were blocked off as the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office set up a command center. Those evacuated were let back inside shortly after.

Not everyone experienced the quake. Students at the Swatch Watchmaking School were evacuated but initially did not understand why. "We literally didn't feel a thing. We thought maybe somebody was messing with them," student Jack Hodapp said. For Juan Cardona, the evacuation's cause was unclear at first. "In the beginning, I thought there was some kind of a criminal scene, or whatever, but no, it wasn't that. Then talking to the people is when I realized there was an earthquake in Cuba, and then somehow impacted this area of Florida," Cardona said. The National Weather Service said there is no tsunami risk as a result of the quake. No injuries have been reported.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie's Southern Grove neighborhood named one of America's fastest-growing areas
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie's 34987 zip code has been named one of the fastest-growing zip codes in the country by RentCafe, driven by the explosive expansion of the Southern Grove neighborhood. A community that barely existed a decade ago, Southern Grove has become a major jobs hub and economic center. The neighborhood has attracted big-name employers including FedEx and Amazon. Amazon is closing its current facility later this year to build an even larger one in the area. Housing inventory in Southern Grove has grown by 177 percent, one of the largest growth spurts in all of Florida. The neighborhood earned high marks for its educated residents and strong homeownership rates.

Southern Grove was deliberately designed as one of four neighborhoods meant to give people compelling reasons to move there and stay. According to Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, Florida's high number of up-and-coming communities reflects the state's favorable tax environment and relatively lower housing costs compared to major markets like New York and California. Sustained infrastructure investment has also fueled construction activity in growing suburbs. Port St. Lucie was not the only Florida community recognized for growth. Ponte Vedra Beach claimed the number one spot on RentCafe's "America's 50 Newest Neighborhoods" list. Daytona Beach and the St. Augustine area also cracked the top 50, earning recognition for their excellent schools and strong housing demand.

cards.headline: Delayed I-95 roadwork causes major rush-hour backups in Martin County
cards.body:
Delayed roadwork on Interstate 95 in Martin County caused significant traffic backups during Tuesday morning rush hour. The construction delays affected northbound and southbound lanes along the I-95 corridor through the county.

Commuters heading to work faced extended travel times as roadwork that was scheduled to be completed remained active during peak traffic hours. The delays forced drivers to navigate through reduced lanes and construction zones during their morning commutes.

The roadwork is part of ongoing infrastructure improvements along the I-95 corridor in Martin County. Traffic patterns were disrupted as crews continued work that extended beyond the planned completion time.

Motorists traveling through Martin County on I-95 during morning and evening rush hours should expect continued delays until the roadwork is completed. Drivers are advised to allow extra travel time when using this route.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County implements 45-day anchoring limit in Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor
hero.body:
St. Lucie County established new anchoring restrictions in two waterway areas beginning June 1. The anchor limitation zones are located in the Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor near the South Causeway Bridge. Under the new rules, boaters cannot anchor a vessel for more than 45 consecutive days within any six-month period in these designated areas. If a boater wants to anchor again after reaching the 45-day limit, they must leave all anchor limitation areas for at least 24 hours before returning.

County officials implemented the restrictions in response to a growing problem with abandoned vessels in these waterways. According to Erick Gill with St. Lucie County, the Fish and Wildlife Commission collected approximately two dozen derelict vessels last year. Gill explained that the new rules will help improve navigation in the area. "We need to make sure that highway for vessels is clear and free for other vessels to come and go," he said. The restrictions aim to prevent vessels from remaining stationary in these waterways for extended periods.

Environmental protection is another key concern driving the new policy. When abandoned vessels remain in the water too long, they can threaten water quality through leaks from diesel tanks, oil tanks, and holding tanks. James Beams with St. Lucie County Port, Inlet and Beaches noted in December that these environmental hazards posed significant risks to the ecosystem. Gill said the anchoring restrictions will help prevent pollutants from entering the water and damaging the lagoon. The Indian River Lagoon supports over 4,000 species of animals, plants, and birds, making it an environmentally sensitive area that requires protection.

The county created these anchor limitation areas to balance the needs of boaters with environmental and navigational concerns. Officials want to ensure the waterways remain accessible for vessels while also protecting the lagoon from the damage caused by long-term vessel abandonment. A site map showing the specific anchor limitation areas is available from the county for boaters who need to understand the exact boundaries of the restricted zones.

cards.headline: Florida property tax referendum faces up to five constitutional challenges
cards.teaser: The referendum to lower property taxes in Florida may face multiple state constitutional challenges, according to a former state senator.
cards.body:
Former Florida state Sen. Jeff Brandes identified five potential constitutional challenges to the property tax referendum approved in special session last week. In a social media post, Brandes outlined concerns regarding ballot language, equal protection, uniformity, home rule and unfunded mandates. The referendum would raise the homestead exemption for homeowners to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028.

State Rep. Toby Overdorf, R-Stuart, emphasized that the measure represents a joint resolution that changes the Constitution rather than a normal bill, which he said makes a legal challenge likely. Multiple lawsuits could strain the courts before Election Day in November. Brandes noted the courts will need to consolidate the challenges and address several complex questions. No lawsuits have been filed against the referendum yet, though legal action is expected once voters receive the final ballot language.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Commissioner Sara Baxter announces run for Congress in District 22
cards.teaser: Sara Baxter will drop out of the commission race to aim for Florida's newly drawn District 22 congressional seat.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County Mayor and District 6 Commissioner Sara Baxter announced on Monday that she will be running for Congress and will drop out of the commission race to pursue the seat. Baxter will aim for Florida's newly drawn District 22 seat, stating that "Washington needs more fighters who are focused on delivering for their district." She added that the new congressional district gives her the opportunity to work with President Trump on priorities including stopping illegal migrant crime, protecting elections, cutting taxes, slashing red tape and bureaucracy, protecting farmers and the food supply chain, supporting the military and veterans, and defending Second Amendment rights.

Baxter was elected to the District 6 seat in 2022 representing parts of western Palm Beach County including Royal Palm Beach, Loxahatchee Groves, Acreage, Wellington, Westlake, Belle Glade, South Bay, Pahokee, and West Lake Worth. A self-proclaimed political outsider, she held no political office before her election to the District 6 seat and previously ran a small business with her husband, Brian. President Donald Trump has endorsed Baxter, calling her "A true MAGA Warrior" and highlighting her work to grow the economy, promote products made in the U.S.A., cut taxes and regulations, advance American energy dominance, stop migrant crime, and support the military, veterans, and law enforcement. Her announcement creates an open race for the District 6 county commission seat, with candidate qualifying still open and additional candidates expected to enter.

James Beams with St. Lucie County Port, Inlet and Beaches explained that diesel tanks, oil tanks, and holding tanks on derelict vessels pose significant environmental hazards. The new restrictions aim to prevent pollutants from these sources from contaminating the lagoon's waters.

The Indian River Lagoon supports an extensive ecosystem containing over 4,000 species of animals, plants, and birds. County officials emphasize that protecting this diverse environment is a priority. The anchoring limitation rules represent one step toward maintaining water quality and habitat conditions for the species that depend on the lagoon. Residents seeking additional information about the designated anchor limitation areas can access site maps from St. Lucie County.

According to police, a preliminary investigation revealed that while family members were inside the residence, the child unlocked a door and left the home unnoticed. When family members realized the child was missing, they searched the property and discovered the child unresponsive in the swimming pool.

Family members immediately began administering first aid until Fort Pierce police officers arrived at the scene. Police worked to save the child, who was then taken to a local hospital for emergency medical treatment. However, the child later succumbed to his injuries. The incident remains under investigation. This drowning is the latest in a series of similar incidents in the region, following a 2-year-old who drowned in a Greenacres canal in March and another 2-year-old who drowned in Palm Beach Gardens in May.

cards.headline: Property tax referendum in Florida faces up to five constitutional challenges before November vote
cards.teaser: Former state Senator Jeff Brandes says the referendum raising homestead exemptions to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028 could face legal challenges on multiple constitutional grounds.
cards.body:
The referendum on lowering property taxes in Florida may face multiple state constitutional challenges before the November Election Day vote, according to former state Sen. Jeff Brandes. In a Saturday social media post, Brandes identified five possible legal challenges: ballot language, equal protection, uniformity, home rule and unfunded mandates. "I think there's questions about home rule. Think there's questions about unfunded mandates. I think there's questions about taxing uniformity. There's a variety of questions," Brandes told WPTV on Monday. The referendum would raise the homestead exemption for homeowners to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028.

State Rep. Toby Overdorf, R-Stuart, emphasized the significance of the measure after it was approved in special session last week. "We need to first of all remember this is not a normal bill. This is a joint resolution that changes the Constitution," Overdorf told WPTV. While Overdorf expects a legal challenge, he expressed concern that multiple challenges could pressure the courts. Brandes said the courts will need to consolidate the cases, stating "They're going to have to consolidate these things down." At this point, no lawsuits have been filed against the referendum, though many expect legal action once the official ballot language is completed.

cards.headline: Delray Beach Golf Club renovation reaches 50 percent completion with November reopening targeted
cards.teaser: The $30 million renovation of Delray Beach Golf Club has reached the halfway point, with city officials saying the project remains on track for completion by the end of 2026.
cards.body:
Delray Beach Golf Club's $30 million renovation is halfway complete as of early June, with city officials on track to finish by the end of 2026 and reopen in November. The course has been closed since November 2025 for the makeover, which aims to restore its historic character while modernizing the facility. The original course was designed by legendary architects Donald Ross and Dick Wilson, and the city is preserving those historic elements. The renovation is happening in phases, with the north nine holes, called the Wilson 9, already fully grassed and growing in, while the south nine holes, the Ross 9, are currently being grassed.

Ronnie Dunayer, a golf instructor who has taught at the course for 20 years, recently toured the progress and said it exceeded her expectations. "I've been an advocate for improvement for a long time, and in all honesty, it's looking better than anticipated," she said. However, not all residents support the changes. Delray Beach resident Maureen Allyn expressed concern about large planting holes being dug for trees near her home that could block her view of the golf course and potentially impact her property's value. The city says the $30 million budget has remained unchanged since work began.

cards.headline: Brightline and Tri-Rail offer transit options for World Cup matches at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens
cards.teaser: Thousands of fans heading to Hard Rock Stadium for the 2026 FIFA World Cup can use Brightline and Tri-Rail transit options to avoid high parking costs that reach up to $200.
cards.body:
Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens will host seven World Cup matches, starting Monday, June 15, when Saudi Arabia takes on Uruguay at 6 p.m. The last Miami match, the third-place match, is scheduled for Saturday, July 18 at 5 p.m. Brightline is the official transit partner for the FIFA World Cup 2026 in Miami, offering round-trip tickets ranging from $76 to $150. From the Brightline Aventura Station, the designated transit hub closest to the stadium, Miami-Dade County will provide free Game Day Express shuttle buses directly to the stadium gates on a first-come, first-served basis. Riders must show a valid World Cup match ticket for that specific day to board.

Tri-Rail offers a more affordable option, with one-way tickets ranging from $2.50 to $6.90 depending on the starting station, and weekend round-trip travel available for $5. Both transit systems are cheaper than driving and parking, with some stadium parking passes costing as much as $200. Additional transit options include Metrorail, Metrobus, and the connection via Metorail or Tri-Rail to the Miami-Dade Golden Glades Interchange and Metrobus Route 297 (Orange Express). Rideshare services like Uber and Lyft can drop passengers at designated rideshare zones at the stadium, though surge pricing and longer wait times are expected, especially after matches.

cards.headline: Four men rescue 324-pound sea turtle in Jupiter Sound
cards.teaser: Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony were boating in Jupiter Sound when they spotted a massive green sea turtle struggling in the Intracoastal Waterway.
cards.body:
Four friends boating in Jupiter Sound spotted a 324-pound adult female sea turtle struggling in the Intracoastal Waterway. Chris DeSousa, Will Savery, Michael Pickett and Tony Anthony quickly realized the injured turtle was too heavy and badly injured for any one person to handle alone. Working together, they carefully tied a rope around the turtle's shell and guided her toward Blowing Rocks Marina. Once they got the turtle, which they named Zoey, out of the water, her shell was covered in deep cuts and her head drooped weakly, telltale signs of a boat strike.

The Loggerhead Marinelife Center responded quickly to the marina and confirmed that Zoey had suffered severe injuries from a vessel strike. Despite the team's heroic efforts and the marine center's care, Zoey passed away just hours later. According to NOAA, hundreds to thousands of sea turtles are struck by vessels in the U.S. every year. In Florida alone, injuries consistent with vessel strikes are observed in 20 to 30 percent of stranded sea turtles. Adult sea turtles are particularly vulnerable to vessel strikes during nesting season, which runs in Florida from March through October.

According to Alexandra Both, a writer for RentCafe, Florida's high number of up-and-coming communities, second only to Texas, reflects the state's favorable tax environment and relatively lower housing costs compared to major markets like New York and California. Sustained infrastructure investment has also fueled construction activity in many of these growing suburbs. Other Florida communities also made RentCafe's recognition list, with Ponte Vedra Beach claiming the number one spot on the "America's 50 Newest Neighborhoods" list. Daytona Beach and the St. Augustine area also cracked the top 50.

hero.headline: Beetlejuice Musical Runs Through June 7 at Kravis Center in West Palm Beach
hero.teaser: The Broadway hit plays through June 7 at the Alexander W. Dreyfoos Concert Hall with actor Ryan Stajmiger in the iconic striped suit. Tickets start at $34.50.
hero.body:
Beetlejuice the musical runs June 2 through June 7 at the Kravis Center in West Palm Beach. The Broadway hit brings its spooky humor, over-the-top visuals, and heartwarming moments to Palm Beach County. Actor Ryan Stajmiger steps into the iconic striped suit to play the mischievous demon beloved from Tim Burton's 1988 film.

The musical follows Lydia Deetz, a strange and unusual teen, whose life changes after meeting two recently deceased neighbors and a demon with a flair for trouble. Stajmiger says one of his favorite parts is laughing with the audience. Very early in the run, he experienced an unexpected moment when he had a wig change on stage and was wearing two wigs. The second wig came off with the first wig, so he was bald for an entire scene.

Performances include 7:30 p.m. shows on June 3 and June 4, 8 p.m. on June 5, matinee and evening performances on June 6, and a closing matinee on June 7. Tickets start at $34.50 and can be purchased directly at kravis.org. The show is recommended for ages 13 and up, with parental discretion advised.

cards.headline: 80-Mile Ocean Paddle From Bahamas to Lake Worth Beach Set for June 13 to Benefit Cystic Fibrosis Families
cards.body:
More than 100 paddlers will cross 80 miles of the open Atlantic Ocean in June for the annual Crossing for Cystic Fibrosis. Event founder Travis Suit said participants will launch from Bimini, Bahamas, at midnight on June 13, arriving at Lake Worth Beach after 12 to 16 hours of paddling. The endurance trek benefits the Piper's Angels Foundation, which Suit established to honor his daughter, Piper, who was diagnosed with cystic fibrosis at age 4. The crossing is part of a four-day schedule beginning June 10 with arrivals and a poolside social at Bimini Cove. On Thursday, participants will take part in a 4Ocean beach cleanup and community buffet dinner. Friday includes a Paddle Out Rose Ceremony to honor cystic fibrosis warriors, followed by rest and safety checks before the midnight launch.

Safety requirements are mandatory for all paddlers, who must wear U.S. Coast Guard-approved personal flotation devices, waterproof whistles, and reflective gear during dark hours. GPS trackers provided by the event must be worn and remain active throughout the journey, and mandatory safety meetings will be held before departure. Paddlers must raise at least $2,000, while crew or virtual participants must raise $500 minimum. All contributions are due by July 31. Spectators are invited to Lake Worth Beach on June 13 to celebrate the paddlers' arrival during a daylong beach celebration. More information is available at crossingforcysticfibrosis.com and pipersangels.org.

hero.headline: Hector Mujica nears exit from Florida's 28th Congressional District race over party registration issue
hero.teaser: Less than two weeks after a brief 2025 party switch was reported to likely bar him from running as a Democrat, Hector Mujica is on the precipice of withdrawing from the race for Florida's 28th Congressional District.
hero.body:
Hector Mujica is preparing to withdraw from the Democratic primary in Florida's 28th Congressional District following a party registration problem that makes him ineligible to run. The former Google executive wants federal prosecutor Robin Peguero, currently running in the neighboring 27th Congressional District, to switch races and take his place, according to multiple sources.

The eligibility issue stems from a party affiliation change in Mujica's voter registration records. Broward County records show that Mujica switched from Democrat to no party affiliation on June 4, 2025, then returned to Democrat on July 26, 2025. Florida law requires candidates to maintain continuous party membership for 365 consecutive days to run for a party's nomination. Democratic lawmakers unanimously passed this requirement earlier this year, and Governor Ron DeSantis signed it into law in April.

Mujica initially claimed the registration change was a clerical error and stated he was unaware of the switch until his opponent's campaign discovered it in late July. However, the Broward Supervisor of Elections rejected this explanation, saying their records review found no evidence of any administrative mistake. Mujica's inability to account for the change is notable given that he had recently run for U.S. Senate, raising over $717,000 before withdrawing about two weeks before that race's qualifying period. Retired Air Force Commander Phil Ehr, Mujica's primary opponent in the district, filed a complaint with the Florida Elections Commission and threatened to file a lawsuit on Friday, the final day of qualifying, if Mujica remains on the ballot.

Ehr's campaign manager Vanessa Brito confirmed that Mujica is attempting to recruit Peguero to replace him in the race. Peguero has raised $800,000 through March 31 and is currently in a Democratic primary against Eliott Rodriguez for the 27th District seat, which is being defended by Republican Maria Elvira Salazar. Brito expressed disapproval of the recruitment effort, saying Mujica should withdraw and wait until he becomes eligible to run. The 28th Congressional District covers portions of southwestern Miami-Dade County, including Florida City, Homestead, South Miami, and Sweetwater, along with the Florida Keys in Monroe County. The 27th District includes Miami, Coral Gables, and several other communities. Federal candidates must reside in Florida but not necessarily in their specific district.

cards.headline: Democratic Sen. Shevrin Jones launches campaign for Florida's 24th Congressional District
cards.teaser: Miami Gardens Democratic Sen. Shevrin Jones has officially launched his campaign for Florida's 24th Congressional District, four days after filing paperwork to run for the seat being vacated by a retiring congressman.
cards.body:
Democratic Sen. Shevrin Jones officially launched his campaign for Florida's 24th Congressional District on Monday evening at Koinonia Worship Center in Pembroke Pines, the church his parents founded. In his announcement, Jones criticized politicians in Washington for prioritizing themselves and wealthy donors while working families struggle with rising costs. His campaign video focused on kitchen-table issues including grocery and gas prices and healthcare bills that are bankrupting families. "Our community deserves someone who understands our struggles, shares our values and wakes up every day focused on lowering costs and creating opportunities for everyday people," Jones said in the video.

Jones made history as the first openly gay person elected to the Florida Senate and could become the state's first LGBTQ member of Congress. He won election to the Florida House in 2012, serving four consecutive terms, before winning his Senate District 34 seat in 2020. He passed legislation including the Dignity for Incarcerated Women act, a blue envelope program to improve police interactions with people on the autism spectrum, and the Teddy Bridgewater Act to allow coaches and boosters to better help students. CD 24 covers Miami Gardens in Miami-Dade and Hollywood, Miramar and Pembroke Park in Broward County, with 68.7% of voters backing Democrat Kamala Harris in 2024. Jones faces opponents including Oliver Gilbert, Rudy Moise, Jean Monestime, and Christine Sanon-Jules. The qualifying deadline is June 12, with the General Election on November 18.

cards.headline: 6.1 magnitude earthquake off Cuba rattles Florida from Miami to Jacksonville, prompts evacuations
cards.teaser: A 6.1 magnitude earthquake struck about 73 miles northwest of western Cuba on Monday afternoon at 2 p.m., rattling residents across Florida from Miami and Fort .
cards.body:
A 6.1 magnitude earthquake off the west-northwest coast of Cuba prompted evacuations of several buildings across Miami on Tuesday and was felt as far north as Jacksonville. Students at Fusion Academy were among those evacuated. "The people that are in the top floors, which they said that they felt it even more than we did," student Maria Torrado said. She described the evacuation alarm as urgent, recalling that staff announced "this is not a drill." Streets near some affected buildings were blocked off as the Miami-Dade Sheriff's Office set up a command center. Those evacuated were let back inside shortly after.

Not everyone experienced the quake. Students at the Swatch Watchmaking School were evacuated but initially did not understand why. "We literally didn't feel a thing. We thought maybe somebody was messing with them," student Jack Hodapp said. For Juan Cardona, the evacuation's cause was unclear at first. "In the beginning, I thought there was some kind of a criminal scene, or whatever, but no, it wasn't that. Then talking to the people is when I realized there was an earthquake in Cuba, and then somehow impacted this area of Florida," Cardona said. The National Weather Service said there is no tsunami risk as a result of the quake. No injuries have been reported.

cards.headline: David Jolly taps Sean Pittman as transition chair ahead of Florida gubernatorial election
cards.teaser: Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Jolly has named Sean Pittman as his transition chair, preparing for potential victory in November's election for Florida Governor.
cards.body:
Sean Pittman, a senior partner of the Pittman Law Group in Tallahassee, will serve as Transition Chair for David Jolly's gubernatorial campaign. Pittman previously served as a top-level campaign adviser to Andrew Gillum's 2018 gubernatorial election and helped propel Gillum to a near-miss victory. Gillum came within 34,000 votes of winning, a 0.4% margin that places the race among the closest in modern American history. As Transition Chair, Pittman will oversee transition planning, including personnel recruitment, policy coordination and strategy development. The announcement follows Monday's news that Jolly had tapped former Democratic gubernatorial candidate Gwen Graham to be his running mate, though the campaign did not confirm that news.

Pittman's selection helps the Jolly campaign prepare strategies to tackle affordability issues including rising housing costs, skyrocketing insurance premiums, rising healthcare costs and other economic pressures facing Florida's working families. Jolly is now the presumptive Democratic nominee for Governor after Orange County Mayor Jerry Demings announced last week he was suspending his campaign. Qualifying for the race doesn't end until Friday, and it won't be clear until then whether Jolly will become the nominee immediately or have to wait until after the Aug. 19 Primary.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Commissioner Sara Baxter enters race for Florida's 22nd Congressional District
cards.teaser: Republican Sara Baxter is forgoing a re-election bid for the Palm Beach County Commission, where she currently serves as Mayor, in favor of running for Florida's 22nd Congressional District.
cards.body:
Sara Baxter is forgoing her re-election bid for the Palm Beach County Commission, where she serves as Mayor, to run for Florida's 22nd Congressional District. She filed paperwork with the Federal Election Commission to run in the redrawn CD 22, which spans parts of Palm Beach and Broward counties and extends through Hendry and Collier counties. She joins other GOP candidates including Deborah Adeimy, Casey Askar, David Burck, Michael Carbonara, Terri Hasdorff, Belinda Keiser, Anna Medvedeva, and Herbert Wertheim. Baxter won her County Commission seat in 2022, flipping District 6 during the red wave tied to Gov. Ron DeSantis' re-election. She represents western Palm Beach County, including Royal Palm Beach, Wellington, Loxahatchee Groves, the Acreage, Belle Glade, and the Glades agricultural region. Prior to public office, she worked in healthcare, taught middle school science, and worked as a real estate agent.

Baxter departs the District 6 race after raising nearly $146,000 through her campaign account, the most of any candidate in the contest. President Donald Trump endorsed her for re-election, calling her a "true MAGA Warrior." CD 22 as redrawn stretches from western Palm Beach and Broward counties through rural Hendry and Collier counties to Marco Island on the Gulf Coast. About 54.6 percent of voters there supported Donald Trump in 2024, though more than 51 percent voted for Joe Biden in 2020. Former high school principal and current Apple strategy manager Pia Dandiya is running on the Democratic side, while Ukraine-born businessman Lev Parnas is running as an independent. The General Election is on Nov. 3.

cards.headline: Charlie Crist raises $1.6 million for St. Petersburg mayoral race, launches major vote-by-mail effort
cards.teaser: St. Petersburg mayoral candidate Charlie Crist raised more than $330,000 from the beginning of April through the end of May, bringing his total haul to more than $1.6 million.
cards.body:
Charlie Crist raised more than $330,000 from early April through the end of May, bringing his total to more than $1.6 million for his St. Petersburg mayoral campaign. The fundraising includes nearly $283,000 raised to his affiliated political committee, St. Pete Shines, and more than $54,000 raised to his official campaign. More than 150 donors have contributed since Crist officially entered the race in late April. Michelle Todd Schorsch, who oversees St. Pete Shines, said the campaign's momentum is clear, citing a significant cash on hand advantage and a bipartisan coalition of small-dollar donors, political committees and businesses. Crist emphasized his commitment to voting access, referencing his restoration of voting rights to approximately 155,000 Floridians with prior felony convictions during his tenure as governor, which he called the largest voting rights restoration by a Florida governor in history.

With early voting beginning Aug. 8 and the mail ballot request deadline set for Aug. 1, St. Pete Shines and Crist's campaign are investing six figures to restore vote-by-mail requests to pre-2021 levels. A 2021 law signed by Gov. Ron DeSantis requires voters to request mail ballots every two years after each General Election. The Tampa Bay Times reported vote-by-mail requests are down across the Tampa Bay region, with some areas seeing requests drop by as much as half. Incumbent Mayor Ken Welch has significantly trailed Crist in fundraising, raising just under $220,000 in the first quarter of 2026 between his campaign and affiliated political committee, St. Pete Progress, with less than $193,000 on hand.

cards.headline: Veteran appellate attorney Andy Bardos joins Shutts & Bowen as partner in Tallahassee
cards.teaser: Veteran appellate attorney Andy Bardos has joined Shutts & Bowen's Tallahassee office as a partner in the firm's Appellate Practice Group, bringing more than two decades of experience handling complex litigation and appeals.
cards.body:
Veteran appellate attorney Andy Bardos has joined Shutts Bowen's Tallahassee office as a partner in the firm's Appellate Practice Group. Bardos brings more than two decades of experience handling complex litigation and appeals for public and private-sector clients, with a practice focused on constitutional, election, redistricting and administrative law matters. His work has included defending the Florida Department of State and county Supervisors of Elections in challenges to state election laws, representing the Florida House in redistricting litigation and defending the Legislature in constitutional challenges involving appropriations. He also served on the legal team representing then-Gov. Rick Scott and the National Republican Senatorial Committee during the closely watched 2018 U.S. Senate recount litigation.

Jack McElroy, firmwide managing partner of Shutts Bowen, said Bardos' experience and reputation in complex constitutional and government-related matters make him an outstanding addition to the firm and strengthen its appellate talent statewide. Daniel Nordby, Chair of Shutts Bowen's Appellate Practice Group, noted that Bardos has handled some of the most closely watched legal matters in Florida over the last two decades and that his depth of experience enhances the firm's ability to guide clients in high-stakes disputes at both the trial and appellate levels. Before entering private practice, Bardos served as Special Counsel to the Senate President, where he worked on legislative development and coordinated policy matters for the Judiciary Committee, Health Regulation Committee and Ethics and Elections Subcommittee. He earned a bachelor's degree, cum laude, from the University of Central Florida and a law degree and Master of Laws in taxation from the University of Florida.

hero.headline: Delayed I-95 roadwork causes major rush-hour backups in Martin County
hero.body:
Delayed roadwork on Interstate 95 in Martin County caused significant traffic backups during Tuesday morning rush hour. The construction delays affected northbound and southbound lanes along the I-95 corridor through the county.

Commuters heading to work faced extended travel times as roadwork that was scheduled to be completed remained active during peak traffic hours. The delays forced drivers to navigate through reduced lanes and construction zones during their morning commutes.

The roadwork is part of ongoing infrastructure improvements along the I-95 corridor in Martin County. Traffic patterns were disrupted as crews continued work that extended beyond the planned completion time.

Motorists traveling through Martin County on I-95 during morning and evening rush hours should expect continued delays until the roadwork is completed. Drivers are advised to allow extra travel time when using this route.

cards.headline: Four Martin County restaurants earn perfect inspection scores while one fails

cards.body:
Four restaurants across Martin County earned perfect scores during recent health inspections conducted by the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation. The establishments met all health and safety requirements during their routine inspections.

One Martin County restaurant failed its inspection, while another was ordered temporarily closed due to violations. The inspections are part of regular health and safety monitoring of food service establishments throughout the county.

All restaurants in Florida are subject to unannounced inspections to ensure compliance with state health codes. Inspection reports are public record and available through the state regulatory agency.

An online poll is seeking votes for the best restaurant in Stuart's Port Salerno area. The poll asks residents and visitors to select their favorite dining establishment in the waterfront community.

Port Salerno is located along the Manatee Pocket in southern Martin County. The area is home to numerous waterfront restaurants and marinas serving both locals and tourists.

The voting poll is collecting responses from the public to determine the most popular restaurant in the Port Salerno dining scene. Results will rank the top establishments based on community votes.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound resident Ann Godzyk dies at age 101
cards.teaser: Ann Dysenchuk Godzyk, a Hobe Sound resident, died at age 101.
cards.body:
Ann Dysenchuk Godzyk of Hobe Sound died in 2026 at the age of 101. Godzyk was born in 1925 and lived in the Martin County community of Hobe Sound.

Hobe Sound is an unincorporated community in southern Martin County along the Atlantic coast. The area is home to both year-round residents and seasonal visitors.

Funeral arrangements and memorial information for Godzyk are being handled through local services. The family is accepting condolences following her death.

hero.headline: St. Lucie County implements 45-day anchoring limits in Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor
hero.body:
St. Lucie County established new anchoring restrictions effective June 1 to address growing concerns about abandoned vessels in local waterways. The county created two anchor limitation areas in the Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor near the South Causeway Bridge. Under the new rules, boaters cannot anchor a vessel for more than 45 consecutive days within any six-month period in these designated areas. Anyone wishing to anchor longer must leave all anchor limitation areas for at least 24 hours before returning.

County officials report that abandoned vessels have become an increasing problem in these waterways. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission collected approximately two dozen derelict vessels from the area last year. Erick Gill with St. Lucie County explained that the new restrictions aim to keep the waterways clear and navigable for all boaters. "We need to make sure that highway for vessels is clear and free for other vessels to come and go," Gill said. The regulations should prevent vessels from sitting idle in these critical waterways and blocking passage for other maritime traffic.

Environmental protection is a primary concern driving the new policy. When abandoned vessels remain anchored for extended periods, they can threaten water quality through leaks and deterioration. James Beams with St. Lucie County Port, Inlet and Beaches noted the hazards posed by abandoned vessels. "There's a lot of environmental concern with the diesel and oil tanks and then holding tanks," Beams said. These contaminants can seep into the water, affecting the lagoon's ecosystem. Gill emphasized that the anchoring restrictions will prevent pollutants from entering the water supply.

The Indian River Lagoon supports a diverse ecosystem worth protecting. Gill noted that over 4,000 species of animals, plants, and birds inhabit the lagoon. By limiting how long vessels can remain anchored without interruption, the county hopes to preserve this vital habitat and prevent environmental degradation. St. Lucie County has made available a site map showing the exact boundaries of the anchor limitation areas for boaters who need to reference the new regulations.

cards.headline: 2-year-old drowns in Fort Pierce swimming pool on Saturday
cards.teaser: A 2-year-old drowned after being found unresponsive in a swimming pool at a home on Citrus Avenue.
cards.body:
A 2-year-old drowned over the weekend in Fort Pierce after being found unresponsive in a swimming pool, police said. The drowning occurred at a home in the 2600 block of Citrus Avenue on Saturday. According to a preliminary investigation, while family members were inside the residence, the child was able to unlock a door and leave the home unnoticed. When they realized the child was missing, family members began searching the property and found the child unresponsive in the swimming pool.

Family members immediately began administering first aid until Fort Pierce police officers arrived at the scene. The officers worked to save the child, who was then taken to a local hospital for emergency medical treatment. However, the child later succumbed to his injuries. Police said the incident remains under investigation. This latest drowning comes after a 2-year-old drowned in a Greenacres canal in March and another 2-year-old drowned in Palm Beach Gardens in May.

St. Lucie County put new anchoring rules into effect on June 1 to address the growing problem of abandoned vessels in local waterways. The county designated two anchor limitation areas in the Indian River Lagoon and Fort Pierce Harbor near the South Causeway Bridge. Under these new restrictions, boaters cannot anchor a vessel for more than 45 consecutive days within any six-month period without leaving all anchoring limitation areas for at least 24 hours. This requirement forces temporary departures that help prevent vessels from becoming permanently abandoned in the water.

The county has experienced an increase in derelict vessels over recent years. According to Erick Gill with St. Lucie County, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission collected around two dozen abandoned vessels last year alone. Gill explained that the new anchoring limitations will improve navigation in these waterways. "We need to make sure that highway for vessels is clear and free for other vessels to come and go," he said. Environmental protection is another key concern driving the new restrictions. James Beams with St.Lucie County Port, Inlet and Beaches noted that long-abandoned vessels pose serious risks to water quality. "There's a lot of environmental concern with the diesel and oil tanks and then holding tanks," Beams said. When derelict vessels remain in the water for extended periods, these fuel and waste systems can leak or fail, contaminating the lagoon. The new 45-day limit helps prevent this pollution from entering the water and damaging the ecosystem.

The Indian River Lagoon supports an extraordinarily diverse ecosystem. Gill emphasized that over 4,000 species of animals, plants, and birds depend on this waterway. By limiting how long vessels can anchor without leaving, the county is taking action to protect this sensitive environment from the pollutants and debris associated with abandoned boats. Boaters who want to anchor in these areas should be aware of the new rules and plan their trips accordingly. A site map showing the exact locations of the two anchor limitation areas is available for reference.

cards.headline: Former Indian River school athletic director sentenced to 10 years in federal prison
cards.teaser: A former athletic director in the Indian River school system received a 10-year federal prison sentence.
cards.body:
A former athletic director in the Indian River school system was sentenced to 10 years in federal prison. The sentencing was reported Monday.

cards.body:
A 2-year-old drowned over the weekend in Fort Pierce after being found unresponsive in a swimming pool, police said. The drowning occurred at a home in the 2600 block of Citrus Avenue on Saturday. According to a preliminary investigation, while family members were inside the residence, the child was able to unlock a door and leave the home unnoticed. When family members realized the child was missing, they began searching the property and found the child unresponsive in the swimming pool.

Family members immediately began administering first aid until Fort Pierce police officers arrived and worked to save the child. The child was transported to a local hospital for emergency medical treatment but later succumbed to his injuries, police said. The incident remains under investigation. cards.headline: Florida property tax referendum faces potential constitutional challenges
cards.teaser: A referendum to lower Florida property taxes may face multiple state constitutional challenges before the November vote.
cards.body:
The referendum on lowering property taxes in Florida may face a state constitutional challenge on several fronts, according to former state Sen. Jeff Brandes. In a Saturday social media post, Brandes listed five possible legal challenges to the referendum that would raise the homestead exemption for homeowners to $150,000 in 2027 and $250,000 in 2028. Those possible legal challenges include ballot language, equal protection, uniformity, home rule, and unfunded mandates. Brandes told WPTV on Monday that he believes there are questions about home rule, unfunded mandates, and taxing uniformity, among a variety of other concerns.

State Rep. Toby Overdorf, R-Stuart, said this is not a normal bill but rather a joint resolution that changes the Constitution. For that reason, Overdorf said he does expect a legal challenge. However, Brandes noted that multiple challenges could put the courts under pressure with a vote scheduled for Election Day in November. Brandes said the courts would have to consolidate these matters down, with a handful of really interesting questions that need to be asked and addressed. At this point, there are no lawsuits filed against the referendum, but many expect that to happen once the actual question for voters is completed.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Commissioner Sara Baxter runs for Congress in newly drawn District 22
cards.teaser: Palm Beach County Mayor and District 6 Commissioner Sara Baxter announced she will run for Congress and drop out of the commission race.
cards.body:
Palm Beach County Mayor and District 6 Commissioner Sara Baxter announced Monday that she will run for Congress in Florida's newly drawn District 22, confirming to WPTV that she will drop out of the county commission race. Baxter, who was elected to the District 6 seat in 2022, represents parts of western Palm Beach County including Royal Palm Beach, Loxahatchee Groves, Acreage, Wellington, Westlake, Belle Glade, South Bay, Pahokee, and West Lake Worth. A self-proclaimed political outsider, Baxter held no political office before her 2022 election. She previously ran a small business with her husband, Brian. President Donald Trump has endorsed Baxter, calling her "A true MAGA Warrior."

Baxter's announcement creates an open race for the District 6 county commission seat. The newly drawn Congressional District 22 is expected to be one of South Florida's closely watched races in the 2026 election cycle. Candidate qualifying has not yet closed, and additional candidates are expected to enter the race.

cards.body: James Bradley of Vero Beach died in 2026. Services are being handled by Strunk Funeral Homes and Crematory in Vero Beach.

cards.headline: Frances Hooker of Vero Beach dies
cards.teaser: Frances Hooker of Vero Beach died in 2026.
